publication_year_note: Published in 2024 in Visnyk of V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University, series 'Geology. Geography. Ecology', Issue 61, pp. 377-391 (Received 3 August 2024; Accepted 9 September 2024; © 2024).
rationale: Full text (15 pages) audited. Based on purposive household survey data (N = 506 households across 25 water supply schemes in Zones I, II and III) and secondary utility records in Guwahati, India, the authors process and tabulate all data in Excel using purely descriptive statistics: plant capacities and production gaps in MLD (Table 1), average days/hours/liters ranges (Table 2), mean water obtained in lpcd by zone (Table 3), mean water quality concentrations in mg/L and NTU (Table 4), household coping strategy percentages (Table 5 and Fig. 4) and percentages of households obtaining adequate water by scheme (Table 6, overall 48.62%). No inferential statistical tests, regression coefficients, correlation coefficients, standard errors, confidence intervals, test statistics or p-values are reported anywhere in the paper. Flagging quantitative_synthesis_eligible = TRUE is therefore overstated.
